title: The City That Owed Tomorrow
premise: Write the opening two chapters of a science-fiction novel. On a floating city that sells its future hours, debt investigator Iona discovers that the evacuation siren has rung in a recording dated tomorrow. A rescue should uncover betrayal or a catastrophic hidden cost. Develop an unsettling planted clue in chapter one and an earned reinterpretation in chapter two. Let a connected shock change what the characters can do next. Avoid recapping completed actions. Each chapter continues actual prior consequences, not its original plan.
pov: Close third-person past tense, one focal character per scene; no head hopping. Dialogue is allowed. Change the focal character only if death makes it necessary.
tone_mood: Tense, strange, emotionally grounded; dangerous decisions with dark wit rather than generic spectacle.
reader_experience: Escalating curiosity and dread, with vivid human costs.

style.register: Precise, vivid contemporary prose. Varied rhythm; let concrete choices carry emotion.
style.interiority: Selective close viewpoint tied to present action.
style.explanation: Trust legible actions; no explanatory moral or recap.

characters.name: Iona
characters.goal: Find who sold the evacuation hours before her district floods.
characters.fear: Discovering her own signature on the sale.

characters.name: Val
characters.goal: Keep the ferry running without exposing an illegal passenger.
characters.voice: Practical, clipped promises; answers a question with a price.

characters.name: Sen
characters.goal: Preserve the city archive while hiding a missing record.

world_rules: Future recordings can show only one possible future; they are not omniscient prophecies.
Time sales cannot resurrect the dead or reverse events already witnessed.
Travel, injuries, custody, debt and individual knowledge persist; secrets require a source.
The ferry has exactly two emergency battery cells at opening; expenditure must be tracked.

initial_facts.text: The ferry has two unused emergency battery cells.
Iona has heard an evacuation siren in a recording dated tomorrow; Val and Sen have not.

plot_design.central_question: Who profits when a city mortgages the hours needed to escape?
causal_dependencies: The recording prompts a specific investigation.
A practical rescue exposes a conflicting obligation.
An earlier clue acquires a new meaning through evidence, not omniscience.

world_design.setting: A floating city of causeways, tide engines, ferries and a guarded municipal time archive.

scene_designs.setting: A floodlit floating berth at rising tide
scene_designs.dramatic_function: Make an urgent rescue choice that costs a tracked resource.
scene_designs.development: Plant a concrete anomalous clue while exposing a competing duty.
scene_designs.restrictions: Do not solve the entire conspiracy or replay the opening recording.
scene_designs.choice_and_consequence: Plant a concrete anomalous clue while exposing a competing duty. A material choice changes available options and imposes a cost.

scene_designs.setting: A checkpoint reachable from the berth with real elapsed travel time
scene_designs.dramatic_function: Continue the actual rescue consequences into a costly confrontation.
scene_designs.development: Reinterpret a planted clue and expose one causal betrayal or catastrophic hidden cost.
scene_designs.restrictions: Carry actual inventory, injuries, knowledge and unresolved obligations from chapter one; no reset.
